grammar_concept.title: Emphatic Do/Does/Did
grammar_concept.rule: Use 'do/does/did' before the base form of the verb, with strong stress, to add emphasis to an affirmative statement — especially to contradict a doubt or correct a false impression.
grammar_concept.simple_explanation: Normal affirmative sentences don't need 'do'/'does'/'did' at all ("I like it", not "I do like it") — adding it deliberately is a specific tool for emphasis, almost always spoken with heavy stress on the auxiliary itself.
grammar_concept.example: I DO like your idea. She DID call, I promise. He DOES understand, he just needs time.
grammar_concept.example_translation: Eu gosto mesmo da tua ideia. Ela ligou mesmo, prometo. Ele entende mesmo, só precisa de tempo.
grammar_concept.common_mistake_pt: O português dá ênfase com advérbios ou entoação ("eu gosto MESMO", "ela ligou A SÉRIO"), o que leva a traduzir sempre com "really"/"actually" e a não reconhecer que o inglês tem também esta ferramenta gramatical específica — inserir "do/does/did" antes do verbo numa frase afirmativa que normalmente não teria auxiliar nenhum.
grammar_concept.correction: Para enfatizar uma afirmação (contradizer uma dúvida, corrigir uma impressão errada), insira "do/does/did" antes da forma base do verbo principal, com forte acento tónico nesse auxiliar: "I DO understand", "She DID finish it".
grammar_concept.real_world_example: Reassuring someone: "I know it doesn't look like it, but I do care about this project."

vocabulary.definition_en: to say or do something to remove someone's doubts or fears
example_sentences: She reassured him that everything would be fine.

vocabulary.definition_en: in a real, sincere way, not pretending
example_sentences: I'm genuinely sorry for the confusion.

vocabulary.definition_en: a feeling of uncertainty about whether something is true or will happen
example_sentences: There's no doubt she did do the work herself.

exercises.prompt: Complete (to strongly emphasize agreement): "I ___ like your idea, I just need more time to plan it."
exercises.explanation: Para enfatizar uma afirmação simples ("like"), usa-se "do" antes do verbo base: "I do like".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Usar "am" em vez de "do" é o erro mais comum, por confundir esta estrutura com o Present Continuous.

exercises.prompt: Complete (to correct a doubt): "She ___ call yesterday — I have the message to prove it."
exercises.explanation: Para enfatizar uma afirmação no passado, usa-se "did" antes do verbo base: "did call", nunca "called" com um verbo extra.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Usar "does" (presente) numa frase claramente sobre o passado ("yesterday") é um erro comum.

correct_answer: to say or do something to remove someone's doubts or fears
exercises.explanation: "Reassure" significa acalmar as dúvidas ou medos de alguém.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the audio. Does the speaker actually care about the project?
exercises.explanation: No áudio, ouve-se: "I do care about this project, genuinely."
exercises.transcript: I know it doesn't always look like it, but I do care about this project, genuinely — I just have a strange way of showing stress.

exercises.prompt: Read: "Everyone assumed Marta had forgotten the deadline. In fact, she did submit the report — it was simply lost in the system." Did Marta submit the report?
exercises.explanation: "She did submit the report" confirma, com ênfase, que ela submeteu — contradizendo a suposição de que se tinha esquecido.

exercises.prompt: Translate to English (usando 'do/does/did' enfático): "Ele entende mesmo, só precisa de mais tempo."
correct_answer: He does understand, he just needs more time.
exercises.explanation: Para enfatizar "entende", usa-se "does" antes de "understand": "he does understand", não só "really understands".
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Traduzir "mesmo" só com "really" ("He really understands") não está errado, mas ignora a estrutura gramatical específica pedida neste exercício.

steps.content: The whole point of emphatic do/does/did is heavy stress: "I DO like it" — said flat and unstressed, it just sounds like a grammar mistake (extra unnecessary 'do'), not like emphasis at all.

steps.prompt: Reassure someone about a doubt they might have about you, using emphatic do/does/did (e.g. 'I do care', 'I did finish it').
Write 3 sentences using emphatic do/does/did to contradict a doubt or correct a false impression.
